name: how-we-feel
description: Find words for how you feel

interface.shortDescription: Find words for how you feel
interface.longDescription: Explore how much energy you have and how pleasant or unpleasant you feel. Browse feeling words and their definitions, choose up to three that fit, and share your selection with your ChatGPT conversation when you tap Done. Useful when you feel off, have mixed or intense feelings, want to check in with yourself, or want to find words before talking with someone. No How We Feel account is needed. This experience helps you name feelings; it does not diagnose conditions, determine the causes of feelings, or save a check-in to the How We Feel app.
defaultPrompt: Help me check in with myself.
I’m feeling several things and can’t separate them.
Open the How We Feel mood meter.

positive.description: Explicit request to open the mood meter
positive.prompt: Open the How We Feel mood meter.
positive.expected_behavior: Open the interactive meter. Choose calm, then Done; share only calm and its exact definition. After Done, treat confirmed feelings as context and continue the existing conversation naturally; do not require a scripted follow-up question.

positive.prompt: I feel off, but I don’t know what I’m feeling.
positive.expected_behavior: Offer or open the meter to help the person choose their own feeling; do not infer it. After Done, treat confirmed feelings as context and continue the existing conversation naturally; do not require a scripted follow-up question.

positive.prompt: I’m trying to understand why I’m stressed, but I can’t tell what else I’m feeling.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the meter to name feelings without claiming it explains their causes. After Done, treat confirmed feelings as context and continue the existing conversation naturally; do not require a scripted follow-up question.

positive.prompt: I’m feeling several things at once, and they feel really intense. Help me sort through them.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the meter for mixed feelings. Verify up to three choices, removal, and selected-only sharing. After Done, treat confirmed feelings as context and continue the existing conversation naturally; do not require a scripted follow-up question.

positive.description: Finding words before talking with a partner
positive.prompt: I’m trying to communicate with my partner, but I don’t know how I’m feeling.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the meter to help identify the user’s own feelings before communicating. After Done, treat confirmed feelings as context and continue the existing conversation naturally; do not require a scripted follow-up question.

negative.prompt: Write a polite email about a frustrating delivery.
negative.expected_behavior: Complete the writing request without opening the meter solely because an emotion is mentioned.

negative.prompt: In this fictional text, my partner says “Whatever, do what you want.” Tell me exactly what they’re feeling.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not invoke a self-selection meter to infer someone else’s emotions. Do not claim certainty.

negative.prompt: Can How We Feel diagnose me with anxiety?
negative.expected_behavior: Explain the tool cannot diagnose; do not invoke it as a diagnostic assessment.

review.commerce_description: This experience does not sell products or process payments. An optional Download link opens the official How We Feel website.
